summary.text: Anthony Marsh is the Liberal MP for Nepean, elected at the May 2026 by-election held after Sam Groth resigned. He was a Mornington Peninsula Shire councillor from 2020 and served as mayor twice. He is standing in Nepean again at the 2026 election.

occupation.text: Aerospace engineer and former RAAF officer; founded a drone-mapping business

summary.text: Darren Hercus is standing for One Nation in Nepean at the 2026 Victorian election. He is a civil engineer who owns a manufacturing business on the Mornington Peninsula. He stood for One Nation at the May 2026 Nepean by-election, finishing second on first preferences with 24.5% before being overtaken on preferences by the independent Tracee Hutchison; the Liberal Anthony Marsh won. One Nation's candidate page refused automated access, so it could not be checked.

prior_roles.role: Owner, joist and truss manufacturing business
prior_roles.note: The ABC describes a joist and truss manufacturer in Dromana; Wikipedia's by-election article describes a fabrication company in Safety Beach.

sources.title: Nepean: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Joseph Toscano is an independent candidate for Nepean at the 2026 Victorian election, on the VEC's list of nominations. According to Wikipedia he is a Melbourne doctor and anarchist activist who has hosted a program on community radio station 3CR since 1977. He has contested many elections since 1990, mostly for the Senate in Victoria, as well as the Melbourne lord mayoralty, Mulgrave at the 2022 state election and Flinders at the 2025 federal election.
summary.note: No source names the Nepean candidate as the doctor and broadcaster of this name described on Wikipedia; the match rests on the name and his record of independent candidacies, including Mulgrave in 2022.

born.note: The article's text gives 1951 but its categories list him under 1952 births.

priorities.text: Direct democracy, including citizen-initiated referendums and a power for voters to recall MPs (his 2007 Senate platform, per Wikipedia)
Defending bulk billing under Medicare, the aim of a community campaign he began in 2003

summary.text: Kim Robbins is running as an independent in Nepean at the 2026 Victorian election. She is a marketer who runs a strategic marketing consultancy, and she moved to the Mornington Peninsula six years ago. Through the community independents movement she became a director and the secretary of Voices of Mornington Peninsula, and she has worked on other independent campaigns.

occupation.text: Marketer; director of a strategic marketing consultancy

priorities.text: Full-time diagnostic services and a fully funded public redevelopment of Rosebud Hospital
Release of the reports behind the rebuilding of part of Peninsula Link, with the answers made public
Funding and recognition for the Peninsula that reflect its regional-style needs rather than a metropolitan label
A single, funded plan for the health of Western Port Bay and its catchment
I answer to Nepean, not a party room.

summary.text: Mike Brown is standing for Family First in Nepean at the 2026 Victorian election. A licensed real estate agent and former small business owner, he has a background in engineering and business and is certified by the Anglican Church as a lay minister and chaplain; he has also been People's Warden at St Mark's in Dromana. He ran for One Nation in the federal seat of Flinders in 2025, and the ABC says he has also been an Australian Christians candidate.

priorities.text: Support for families and children
Protection of religious freedom and freedom of speech and conscience
More choice for parents in their children's schooling
Greater government accountability and less public debt
Help for small business and job creation

summary.text: Seth Willcocks is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Nepean in 2026. He works as a concreter and says he has spent his whole life in the Nepean area. His campaign calls for more spending on public schools and hospitals and for essential services to be returned to public ownership.

priorities.text: More money for public education, plus extra hospital beds and health workers
Returning essential services and resources to public hands
Relief from rising rents, grocery prices and other living costs

summary.text: Sianan Healy is the Greens candidate for Nepean in 2026, after standing for the party in the seat's May 2026 by-election, where she ran fourth with 9.4% of the primary vote. She manages a team at Women's Health Victoria focused on evidence and capacity building, and previously did qualitative research on people's experience of infertility and its treatment. She has a doctorate in history from the University of Melbourne.

occupation.text: Women's health advocate; manager at Women's Health Victoria

prior_roles.role: Manager, Evidence and Capacity Building team

priorities.text: Climate action and social justice as the centre of her Nepean campaign
Listening to and standing up for everyone in the Nepean community
Help for Peninsula families under pressure from bills and rent

summary.text: Surbhi Snowball is standing for Labor in Nepean at the 2026 Victorian election. According to the ABC she was born in Mauritius, arrived in Australia in 2000 and settled on the Mornington Peninsula about a decade ago; her working life has included running a business, farm work and, now, a job in finance. She has stood for Labor before, in the federal seat of Flinders in 2022, where she lost to the Liberal candidate.

summary.text: Tamara Champion is the Animal Justice Party's candidate for Nepean at the 2026 Victorian election, as her party page and the ABC both list her. An environmental scientist from the Mornington Peninsula with a Deakin University degree, she has spent about ten years on bushland restoration work. Wikipedia lists her first on the party's South-Eastern Metropolitan Region upper-house ticket, citing an earlier version of the same party page.

priorities.text: Stronger legal protection for animals and an end to needless suffering
Looking after the Mornington Peninsula's bushland, wildlife and threatened ecosystems
Treating community wellbeing and a healthy environment as linked goals
